interfaces.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.

interfaces.name: Root air drying
interfaces.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
interfaces.costs: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crushed compatible food needs one transfer round, with its prior costs and composition preserved. Unload/dismantle: one round and one energy. Passive weather exchange costs no actor rounds.
interfaces.effects: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at original water. At fraction <=0.12 decay is 0.35 baseline, otherwise crushed food is 1.25 baseline. Exposure continues after unloading. No lost nutrients, reverse spoilage, sterilization or free materials.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

personalIntent.progress: Root air drying is mastered; no stone, bark or tray has been obtained. One root remains in inventory.

evidence: Root air drying is personally mastered.

shown.uncertainty: Current stone stock, bark access and practical preservation benefits remain unverified.

completedSteps: Gathered three roots and ate two.
Read and mastered root air drying.
outputs: Personal mastery of root air drying.
shown.missing: Two stones, one bark, a tray, fresh trial roots and measured drying results.
shown.next: Eat the remaining root and approach the remembered rock using an offset coordinate before gathering.
shown.benefit: Root meals supplied 14 nutrition each; no preservation benefit has been demonstrated.

shown.subject: Tool sources for root preparation
shown.text: Have you personally observed a reachable stone or bark source? I am investigating a small root-crushing trial; I have no tools yet. Crushing itself does not preserve roots.

shown.subject: Root drying limitations and my exploration
shown.text: I read the drying contract: preservation applies only at water fraction <=0.12; rain can reverse drying, and wet crushed roots decay at 1.25 baseline. I will inspect the remembered hazelnut plant nearby rather than duplicate your drying study. No materials or trial results yet.

shown: Known safe foods: root provides 14 nutrition and berry 8; both have toxicity 0.
The rock location and stock are dated tick 7, not current confirmation.
Bark access and preservation benefits remain unverified.
